# Liberal Democrats 1997 Manifesto Summary: "Make the Difference"

## Core Philosophy

The Liberal Democrats position themselves as advocates for a "fair, free and open society" balancing liberty, equality and community. They reject what they characterise as Conservative-induced division and Labour's timidity, presenting themselves as willing to make difficult choices and explain their costs—"a menu with prices."

## Education: The Top Priority

The party commits £2 billion annually in additional education funding, financed by raising income tax by 1p. Key pledges include:
- Universal early years education for 3-4 year olds
- Reducing primary class sizes to maximum 30 pupils
- Doubling school book/equipment spending
- Establishing a General Teaching Council
- Creating Individual Learning Accounts for lifelong learning
- Introducing a training levy on employers

## Economic Vision

The manifesto embraces market economics whilst acknowledging its limitations, advocating:
- Bank of England independence for monetary stability
- Support for joining the single European currency (subject to referendum)
- Regional Development Agencies
- Small business support including statutory interest on late payments
- A "Benefit Transfer Programme" converting unemployment benefits into employer incentives

## Environmental Commitment

A distinctive emphasis on ecological taxation—shifting burdens from jobs to pollution:
- 30% carbon dioxide reduction target over 15 years
- National Homes Insulation programme
- Fuel duty increases offset by car tax reductions
- Investment in public transport and railways

## Constitutional Reform

Extensive democratic modernisation proposals:
- Proportional representation for all elections
- Scottish and Welsh Home Rule with tax-varying powers
- Freedom of Information Act
- Bill of Rights incorporating European Convention on Human Rights
- House of Lords reform toward elected chamber
- Reducing MPs by one-third

## Health and Welfare

NHS commitments include £540 million additional annual investment, 10,000 extra nurses, six-month maximum waiting times, and restored free eye/dental checks. Welfare reform focuses on breaking poverty traps whilst maintaining safety nets.

## Funding Transparency

The manifesto explicitly details financing: 1p income tax rise for education; new 50p rate on incomes over £100,000 funding tax threshold increases; tobacco duty rises funding health checks.
